key_insight: AutoSynthesis turns meta-analysis into an automated, end-to-end agentic workflow. It aims to reduce the manual effort needed to search, screen, and synthesize scientific evidence from natural-language research questions.
problem_solved: Traditional quantitative evidence synthesis is slow, labor-intensive, and hard to scale because it requires manual literature search, study screening, eligibility checks, and data extraction.
method: Uses a multi-agent system that starts from a natural-language research question.
Automatically formulates a search strategy and retrieves relevant scientific literature.
Screens candidate studies, checks full-text eligibility, and extracts data for meta-analysis.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this points to a way to automate a core research workflow that often blocks rapid evidence-based decision-making. If reliable, it could accelerate systematic reviews, improve reproducibility, and help teams synthesize large bodies of literature faster.
visual_elements: End-to-end pipeline diagram: question -> search -> screening -> eligibility -> extraction -> meta-analysis
Multi-agent architecture graphic showing specialized agents and their roles
Before/after comparison of manual vs automated evidence synthesis time and effort
Icon set for literature search, document screening, full-text review, and statistical synthesis
paper_title: AutoSynthesis: An agentic system for automated meta-analysis
paper_authors: Moein Taherinezhad, Sebastian Maier, Gerardo Vitagliano, Francesco Pierri, Stefan Feuerriegel
